results.note: ingest/backfill.py run_backfill takes indicator_key (None means all) and calls recipes[entry.backfill_recipe]. The named test proves one key reaches only its own recipe and is persisted with origin 'backfill'. test_backfill_entry_point_can_run_all_registered_backfillable_keys (line 167) covers all-keys mode and shows not_backfillable entries are skipped. The CLI and .github/workflows/backfill.yml call the same entry point.

The integration marker is gone. A grep for 'integration|pytestmark' in the test file and conftest finds nothing, so the default `uv run pytest -q` gate runs this test. It calls the real run_backfill, which goes through the real persist_board and then persist_datapoint (the origin forwarding at ingest/pipeline.py). The database is a throwaway Postgres schema built from the real migrations, matching the pattern in test_persist_board.py. The test asserts the row lands under the (indicator_key, asset, source_vendor, source_timestamp) identity with origin='backfill'. If the fixture failed to connect it would raise, so the gate's exit 0 means the test passed.

The test runs run_backfill twice against real Postgres, then asserts that exactly one datapoints row exists for the identity and that both runs return that same row id. There is no fake dedup. The test now runs in the default offline suite, which exited 0.

assert_backfill_coverage in ingest/registry.py raises an AssertionError naming the entry when it has neither backfill_recipe nor not_backfillable, or has both. The test asserts the message matches 'silent_indicator'. A companion test at line 294 covers an entry that names an unregistered recipe. run_backfill runs the check before any write.

The test loads the real registry.yaml. It asserts that sol_active_addresses and sol_staking each declare not_backfillable with distinct, source-specific reasons (getBlock and Validators.app). It then asserts that assert_backfill_coverage passes on the full real registry.
The US-903-C6 gate `uv run pytest -q` exited 0, and the mypy --strict typecheck gate also exited 0.

note: Attempt 3 removed the wrong @pytest.mark.integration marker, so the real-Postgres rerun test now runs in the default gate and directly proves the shared write path and idempotency. Every backfillable entry still points at a placeholder 'noop' recipe; that is infrastructure scope, which the story allows. The committed gates.json shows 357 passed / 67 deselected, which does not obviously match the marker being removed, so that evidence file may be stale.
